rule.bands: A above 90%; B+ above 82.5% to 90%; B above 75% to 82.5%; C+ above 66.67% to 75%; C above 58.33% to 66.67%; C- above 50% to 58.33%; D above 25% to 50%; F up to 25%
rule.rank: percentile rank = (scores below + half the ties) / population size; the population of an item is every stock holding a score on that item from its registered run (or its published memo)
rule.registered_run: the newest live card in the conveyor's trays whose run holds scores; dry, cancelled and control runs never enter
rule.boundaries: per item, the lowest score that earned each grade today; null where no score earned that grade
rule.comparison_set: the stocks analysed by the new approach (the Sets of Questions/Items approach)

Q:1:C-01.title: To what extent is end-market demand changing, structurally or cyclically, and with how much visibility? (A cyclical swing counts when it has two-plus years of visibility.)

Q:1:C-02.title: To what extent, and in which direction, is competitive intensity changing?

Q:1:C-03.title: To what extent is a disruption force strengthening or being disproved, and in which direction does it act on the company?

Q:1:C-04.title: To what extent is political or regulatory change under way, and how does it bear on the company?

Q:1:C-05.title: How are input costs, input availability and supplier concentration changing, and is the net effect a headwind or a tailwind?

Q:1:C-06.title: Where is the company's own revenue and demand cycle, and to what extent is it turning?

Q:1:C-07.title: To what extent is a macro force acting on the company, on its sector and on its industry, and at which level does it bite hardest?

Q:1:C-08.title: To what extent is a key driver at the industry or sector level accelerating the company's demand?

Q:1:C-09.title: What other material external dynamic, positive or negative, is at work?

Q:1:C-10.title: Taking each sector and industry thematic driver in turn, and then all of the above together: how strong are the external headwinds and how strong are the tailwinds at value-chain, industry and sector level, and what is the overall external change picture?

Q:1:C-11.title: To what extent have the chief executive, or other key leaders (e.g. finance director, operations director, board, division heads, etc.) or other key actors (e.g. activists, major shareholders) changed, and what does the change signal?

Q:1:C-12.title: To what extent have the strategy or the strategic priorities changed, and how well is the change articulated and resourced? (choices)

Q:1:C-13.title: To what extent has financial guidance been raised, or have mid-term targets or capital-markets-day ambitions been set or raised? (choices)

Q:1:C-14.title: To what extent are standards improving in execution, operational measures, governance or cost discipline? (choices and actions)

Q:1:C-15.title: To what extent is the company reducing its perimeter or composition, through divestments, simplification or exits from low-return units? (actions)

Q:1:C-16.title: To what extent is the company entering new geographic or product markets, and how sensibly? (actions)

Q:1:C-17.title: To what extent is the company raising prices in real terms (above cost inflation), and are the rises real, merely nominal, or so far only latent or plausible and increasingly noted by management? (actions)

Q:1:C-18.title: To what extent is the company stepping up mergers and acquisitions, and how strategically sensible, disciplined and well integrated are they? (actions)

Q:1:C-19.title: To what extent is the company making more use of its balance sheet (for investment, acquisitions or returns), or stepping up shareholder returns (a buyback starting or increasing, a special or progressive dividend), or is management increasingly mooting either? (actions)

Q:1:C-20.title: What other material positive corporate change forces are present/plausible?

Q:1:C-86.title: What negative corporate change developments are present/plausible?

Q:1:C-87.title: To what extent have key controlling actors (e.g. activists, major shareholders) indicated scope for change in strategy/approach?

Q:1:C-21.title: Taken together, how strong, broad and well-resourced are the positive corporate changes under way?

Q:1:C-24.title: Where does the company rank by market share or size for its activity or product, and how far is it from the number one or two position?

Q:1:C-25.title: How concentrated is the market: do the top five hold more than 30 percent, and how steep is the share distribution (for example, do the top five hold five times the share of numbers six to ten)?

Q:1:C-26.title: How stable are market shares over time, and what share have new entrants taken over the last three to five years?

Q:1:C-27.title: To what extent does market share consolidate over time towards the largest competitors, and towards the most advantaged ones (not necessarily the largest or most established), and is this company among them?

Q:1:C-28.title: What is competitors' attitude to competition: do they put margin and return on capital first, or volume first; are they benign and cooperative, or willing to suffer losses; and do industry prices fall when volume falls?

Q:1:C-29.title: How stable is that attitude, and how has it changed over the last eighteen months to three years: do competitors show 'Michael O'Leary' instability (hard to predict, situation-dependent, reactive), and would they launch a 'shark attack' on industry pricing if they sensed weakness?

Q:1:C-31.title: Taken together, how supportive is the industry structure, and how fragile is that support?

Q:1:C-84.title: What do historical precedents, rules of thumb and the empirical evidence show about how companies in this sector and industry have typically generated share price, financial and operational outperformance, and underperformance, and to what extent does this company fit those patterns?

Q:1:C-32.title: How is customer demand behaving: to what extent does it support the thesis, and how fragile is that support?

Q:1:C-33.title: To what extent are the route to market and the intermediaries helping or hindering the company, and how fragile is that?

Q:1:C-34.title: How are existing competitors behaving, does that help or hurt the company, and how fragile is the company's position against them?

Q:1:C-35.title: To what extent are new entrants (from adjacent markets; standard entrants; orthogonal or innovative entrants) entering or threatening this market, and how much of a threat is each type?

Q:1:C-36.title: To what extent are substitutes or alternatives (other ways for customers to solve the problems the company's products solve) a threat, and how is that changing?

Q:1:C-37.title: What are regulators and political actors doing, does it help or hurt the company, and how fragile is that position?

Q:1:C-38.title: On whom in the value chain are disruption forces acting (demand, competition, regulators and political actors, suppliers, any other actor), how is each acting, and how fragile do they leave the company's position?

Q:1:C-39.title: Where relevant or material, how are suppliers behaving: a support to the company, or a source of risk?

G:1:Industry and Value Chain.title: Group judgement: Industry and Value Chain

Q:1:C-41.title: Which sustainable relative competitive advantages or moats does the company hold (customer-related; production-related; scale-based; regulatory or political; culture or knowledge), how strong is each, and are they widening or narrowing?

Q:1:C-42.title: How large is the company's scale relative to competitors and other actors (revenue, headcount and so on), and what does that scale confer?

Q:1:C-43.title: How large is the realistic total addressable market relative to the company, and what rate of growth does it allow for over the mid term?

Q:1:C-44.title: How high is the company's surplus customer utility against competing or alternative offerings, and is it leading, or at least demonstrably not inferior? (Hard to prove, easier to disprove; the aim is to disprove inferiority at Early-Stage and Deep Dive, for example Sophos, Bytes.)

Q:1:C-45.title: To what extent does the company have, and use, demonstrable pricing power with minimal erosion of its relative surplus customer utility, shown by evidence of application rather than conjecture?

Q:1:C-46.title: To what extent does the company share its scale economies with customers, stated or de facto, in its messaging, strategy, culture or values?

Q:1:C-47.title: To what extent do gravitational or mechanical forces, rather than heroic company dynamism, improve the company's competitive advantage and its financial outputs against peers with each period that passes?

Q:1:C-49.title: What earnings-per-share growth is the company generating, with what revenue growth, and how durable is it?

Q:1:C-50.title: How much immediate scope is there to deploy capital or operating spend at a high return on new invested capital for three to five years, and what does that mean for mid- and long-term potential and the fair multiple?

Q:1:C-51.title: How high are the returns on capital: post-tax return on new invested capital, on capital employed and on tangible capital?

Q:1:C-52.title: How high is the conversion of net income into free cash flow, and how do net working capital and similar items behave?

Q:1:C-53.title: How high are gross and operating profit margins, and how are they trending?

Q:1:C-54.title: How clean is the earnings base: how large is the gap between adjusted and reported earnings; do one-offs, capitalised costs or other items flatter it; and does the tax rate or any other non-obvious leakage erode earnings per share?

Q:1:C-75.title: How material is the fixed-cost operating leverage: how much does a given change in revenue move operating profit, and how wide a range of outcomes does that create?

Q:1:C-76.title: How material is the financial leverage or gearing: how much does it amplify earnings per share and risk, and how comfortable is it?

Q:1:C-77.title: How much of each major part of the cost base is cuttable or reducible?

Q:1:C-78.title: Beyond cutting costs, how much plausible scope is there to improve the financial outputs over the mid term; do peer precedents show it is achievable; would it come from a few big areas or many small ones; and is it congruent with the stated strategy?

Q:1:C-79.title: How narrow is the business perimeter (number of countries and business lines), how is it changing, and what does that mean for predictability?

Q:1:C-55.title: How big is the company's ambition or vision (a force: growth as a priority, outcompeting, innovating, adapting, pushing), particularly in relation to peers?

Q:1:C-56.title: How great and smart is the strategy, with right and bold strategic priorities (an enabler): widening the moat over the mid term, growth as a priority, and a dynamic strategy that can capitalise on a plausible range of environments?

Q:1:C-57.title: How great is the chief executive, judged by actions rather than conjecture (an enabler, not an ossifier)?

Q:1:C-57b.title: How high a priority is hiring well for the chief executive, and how great is the leadership team the chief executive has built (an enabler)?

Q:1:C-58.title: How well resourced and invested is the whole business (a buffer; an ant colony: built yesterday for resilience)?

Q:1:C-59.title: How holistic and congruent is the culture, with alignment across the total system (as at Lifco, Avanza or Ryanair)? Such that the goals, strategy, culture, execution, decisions are congruent, holistic and symbiotic?

Q:1:C-60.title: How clear, straightforward and helpful is the company's communication, including on the strategy and the driver transmission mechanism?

Q:1:C-61.title: How strong is the company's record of acting, not just talking: a recent record of huge delivery and action, and a mid-term track record of delivery, not misses or justifications, whatever the environment (outperforming in tougher ones is even better), beyond its records against guidance and estimates?

Q:1:C-62.title: To what extent does the company hold outlier standards, driving higher, faster and better, with a record of out-executing competitors?

Q:1:C-63.title: Explain, with the evidence, the extent to which the company puts shareholders first, ahead of management, and how prudent its governance is (scaffolding put in place even where it was not needed): what does the evidence show, and why?

Q:1:C-64.title: To what extent is the company an enlightened capital allocator and a dynamic repurchaser of its shares, not just an operator or generator, with a record of allocating capital at a high return on new invested capital?

Q:1:C-80.title: To what extent has the core growth engine decelerated over the last twelve months: is the revenue growth rate running below the company's own normal rate, and is the input change force itself slowing?

Q:1:C-81.title: What fundamental risks are there that are sudden, high-magnitude and low-probability, and how plausible and how large is each?

Q:1:C-82.title: What perception- or sentiment-driven risks are there that are sudden and high-magnitude, including events elsewhere in the sector, theme or market that could hit the share price whatever the company's own fundamentals?

Q:1:C-83.title: How far could the shares fall to a fair trough multiple?

Q:1:C-68.title: To what extent is company guidance above or below sell-side consensus for this financial year and next financial year, and why?

Q:1:C-70.title: Beyond meeting or beating, what is the record, nature and behaviour of the company and its chief executive in upgrading guidance?

Q:1:C-71.title: How conservative is current guidance for the next one to three years against the last one to five years, adjusted for the difference in input change forces versus the past?

Q:1:C-72.title: How specific is the guidance: built from stated building blocks, or vague about how results come about?

Q:1:C-85.title: To what extent is informal/qualitative company commentary above or below formal guidance and sell-side consensus for this financial year and next financial year, and why?

Q:1:C-73.title: What else is material or uncommon about the company's guidance or investor relations?

Q:1:C-67.title: How do the sell-side's forecasts for the next one to three years compare with the last one to five years, for the main financial statement line items in particular and the granular working up to them, and how credible is the gap given the change forces and foundations found above?

Q:1:C-69.title: What is the company's record of missing, meeting or beating guidance and sell-side estimates over the last one, three and five years, including in comparable environmental conditions?

Q:1:C-74.title: To what extent have sell-side estimates been cut deeply and fully across all analysts, and has company guidance recently been rebased lower, or more aggressively kitchen-sinked or sandbagged?

Q:1:C-22.title: What staircase of novel positive developments lies ahead: which new, dated things can the market look forward to within the next 6 months, in months 6 to 18, and in months 18 to 36; how novel is each; and how well-founded?

Q:2:P-01.title: After assessing the fixed-cost operating leverage in greater detail, how is it likely to shape the main financial line items over the next 18 months to four years, against the last four to six years?

Q:2:P-02.title: After assessing the financial leverage in greater detail, how is it likely to shape earnings per share and the balance sheet over the next 18 months to four years?

Q:2:P-03.title: After assessing the scope for cost elimination and efficiency in greater detail, how much is likely to reach the main financial line items over the next 18 months to four years, and when?

Q:2:P-04.title: After assessing the pricing power in greater detail, how is price likely to contribute to revenue and margin over the next 18 months to four years?

Q:2:P-05.title: After assessing in greater detail whether reinforcing or balancing feedback loops are at work in the business model, such that dynamics at play today create additional scope for further positive/negative dynamics in the near/mid-term (reinforcing feedback loops), or the opposite (balancing loops), how are they likely to shape the main financial line items over the next 18 months to four years?

Q:2:P-06.title: After assessing the track record of delivery in greater detail, how much weight should the forecasts for the next 18 months to four years carry, and in which direction should they be leaned?

Q:2:P-08.title: After assessing below-operating-profit cost items (e.g. tax, interest, one-offs, minority investments, etc.) and share buybacks or issuance in greater detail, how is it likely to shape earnings per share, net income and free cash flow over the next 18 months to four years, versus the last four to six years?

Q:2:P-09.title: After assessing the other questions/items in the set in greater detail, what is the net likely impact to the main financial line items over the next 18 months to four years, versus the last four to six years?

Q:2:P-10.title: Pulling together all the above answers, in all sets so far, what is your carefully considered base case for the key operational drivers and the key financial line items over the next 18 months to four years?

Q:34:D-01.title: How congruent are the answers to all the questions in the earlier sets: to what extent do they support and align with each other, rather than contradict or jar?

Q:34:D-02.title: To what extent does past and present fundamental delivery make the expected change plausible, and to what extent does the thesis rely only on strengths the business demonstrably has, rather than on strengths it would need to acquire?

Q:34:D-03.title: In relation to the differences between the forecasts over the next 18 months to four years, vs. the last four to six years' financials, how diffuse or concentrated are the key drivers that generate the differences?

Q:34:D-04.title: How wide is the cone of plausible outcomes over the next 18 months, how skewed is it, and so how predictable is the case?

Q:34:D-05.title: How helpful is the company's disclosure on operating momentum and key drivers of the thesis to monitor the case over about the next six months?

Q:34:D-06.title: How clearly does what the company says it will achieve trace into specific operational drivers, onto identifiable revenue, cost and margin lines (the key fundamental milestones and measures), and through to earnings per share; and how clear is the external transmission from value-chain dynamics to earnings per share?

Q:34:D-07.title: To what extent do the share price and the multiple move with sector and industry peers rather than idiosyncratically (on a rolling six-month basis), and so how far is the multiple company-driven rather than industry-driven?

Q:34:I-01.title: How likely is company guidance to be raised, met or reduced at the next few earnings events (all such events over the next 18 months), and what would drive each outcome? Secondarily, how likely is any guidance, mid-term target or ambition for 18 months to three years out to be raised, met or reduced?

Q:34:I-02.title: How likely are sell-side consensus forecasts, and the net breadth of revisions, to move higher or lower over the next few earnings events (over the next 18 months): to be upgraded, cut or held, and why? Secondarily, how likely are the consensus forecasts for 18 months to three years out to be upgraded, cut or held?

Q:34:I-03.title: How comprehensively are these dynamics articulated in the current narrative of (i) sell-side commentary and (ii) investor commentary (for example on Twitter): how well known is each of them to investors who own or cover the company or its sector, primarily for the next 18 months and secondarily for 18 months to three years out?
